paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Moses knows he is about to die, and he spends his last words blessing everybody else. Before he names a single tribe, he starts with the LORD, who came from Sinai with "flaming fire at His right hand" (Deuteronomy 33:2). Every blessing in this passage flows out of who God is, and that's where blessings come from.

Look at how different the blessings are. Judah gets help against his foes (Deuteronomy 33:7), and Benjamin gets to rest on God's shoulders (Deuteronomy 33:12). Asher gets the "most blessed of sons" treatment (Deuteronomy 33:24). Moses speaks a blessing that fits each tribe he names, and that's good news for you too, baker.

Then Moses puts down the list and comes back to the LORD: "The eternal God is your dwelling place, and underneath are the everlasting arms" (Deuteronomy 33:27). Israel is called "a people saved by the LORD" (Deuteronomy 33:29). They didn't earn the blessing. They were carried. I spent years at the bottom of a junk drawer, and I can tell you being carried beats climbing out on your own. And Moses' story isn't over yet.
